The process is crucial for preventing heartdiseases and removing a broad range of newly invented drugs' after consumption effects. This paper introduces some specific machine learning approaches for classifying drugs that could be harmful enough to cause QT syndrome investigating some ECG reports. The proposed method uses basic features, such as PR, RR, QRS and a range of other properties found in ECG description of the target group. Regression and classification based machine models have been developed to learn the properties of ECG and test the model on an independent dataset. Among the proposed algorithms gradient boosting regression model performed better (RMSE = 0.3) while bragging learning based classifier have shown 89% accuracy indicating the potential of machine learning based approach in identifying the drugs crucial for QT distortion.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Cost Blood Pressure Measuring Device
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) is one of the most significant fundamental parameters of cardiac and vascular conditions of human body. Till present, many techniques and devices have been developed to measure and monitor the BP and a variety of different BP measurement devices used in the hospitals and pre-hospital settings. People can measure their BP by using their own electronic devices. But in developing countries, automated BP measurement devices are scarce and expensive. To measure manually using Stethoscope and Sphygmomanometer is the most accurate and inexpensive BP measurement method. But it requires a trained person for measurement accuracy. In most of the electronic BP measurement devices use the oscillometric method. In this paper, we have reported about a microcontroller based low-cost BP measurement device that is able to measure the BP using a hand cuff. The device comprises mainly three parts, such as, hardware (viz. hand-cuff, pressure valve and LCD screen), electronic interface circuit and a microcontroller unit. Test results show good agreement with the results obtained by using conventional BP measurement device.

articleTitle: Spatio- Temporal Analysis of Large Air Pollution Data
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Air pollution is one of the most dangerous environmental threats in our planet. Although it is severe in highly populated and industrialized cities of the developing countries, it is a major concern for developed countries as well. In the developed world, air quality data is gathered from a large number of air pollution monitoring stations. However, the volume of data is very high and it is not possible to analyze the data efficiently in real-time using the conventional methods. Hence, large scale data mining techniques can help in analyzing those data more efficiently and dynamically. In this paper, a method for mining large amount of air pollution data is proposed for finding air pollution hot spots and time of pollution using clustering methods and time-series analysis. The results, after using the method to the air pollution data of PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>.<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>, PM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sub>and ozone in the United Kingdom from 2015-17, has shown that the pollution due to particulate matters was higher in winter season and ozone pollution had downward trend except some areas.

articleTitle: Comparative Assessment of Non-Isolated DC-DC Converters Combined with Passive Ripple Cancelling Circuit
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Extreme frequency utilizations instinctively evolve current ripples in switching power converters, whichever may induce a crucial impression on the output power. Aforementioned ripple current conceives filtering complications, control concerns, output voltage disorder as well as more obstacles. In this study a dynamic passive ripple cancelling circuit (PRCC) is observed, which is used to erase current ripples of the converters. BOOST, CUK, SEPIC and a modified version of SEPIC converters are adopted to explore the efficacy of this ripple eliminating technique. It is detected that by integrating PRCC into the conventional converters, appearing peak to peak input current ripple is declined and ripple eliminating proportion is beyond 97% for all the studied circumstances. The survey is performed depending on steady state evaluation and simulation. MATLAB/SIMULINK mechanism is used to achieve simulated outcomes. However, comparative assessment is executed to determine foremost performing DC-DC converter incorporated with PRCC.

articleTitle: Prediction of Origin of Replication in Genome Using DNA Sequence Based Features
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Origin of replication (OriC) within prokaryotic and eukaryotic genomes are single or several sequences in the genome where DNA double helix strands start unwinding and the replication starts by providing access to the DNA polymerase. Knowledge about OriC is of great importance due to its effect in DNA replication, which is the most important task during cell division. In this paper, we propose a novel method for prediction of OriC in genome sequences. Our proposed supervised learning based method uses simple k-mer features derived from DNA sequences and Support Vector Machine as classification algorithm. Our method is trained using a standard benchmark dataset and on cross fold validation it achieves 84.36% accuracy which is significantly improved than the state-of-the-art methods. It also performs well on other metrics such as Mathew's Correlation Coefficient (MCC), Sensitivity and area under receiver operating characteristic curve (auROC) whose values respectively are 0.69, 0.8621 and 0.8907 and thus is superior in performance compared to the previous state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of Modular Multilevel Converter Based Solid State Transformer Implementing Hybrid Control
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A Solid State Transformer (SST) consists of a high-frequency transformer and power electronic converters. It is relatively a complex system. It requires control in many stages. The control methods vary from topology to topology. In this paper, Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) topology is used in converter stage. To control MMC, a hybrid control is implemented consisting of a modified sorting algorithm and model predictive control. Using the proposed algorithm, the performance of the system under different grid disturbances has been analyzed.

articleTitle: Effect of Gate Bias on Graphene Channel of G4-FET and Gate-All-Around MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, the effect of gate bias using potential distribution for Graphene channel Four Gate Transistor (G4-FET) and Gate-All-Around (GAA) MOSFET have been shown. Potential distribution is obtained by solving 2-D Poisson equation using COMSOL with MATLAB. The potential profile for G4-FET and GAA MOSFET have also been compared.

articleTitle: Role of HVDC Interconnection for Improving Frequency Response in a Low Inertia Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The target of this research work is to investigate the role of High Voltage DC (HVDC) interconnection for enhancing frequency response in a low inertia grid. In recent times, installed capacity of wind and photovoltaic (PV) sources has significantly increased in South Australian power system. Most of these wind power plants deploy variable speed wind machines, whereas PV sources are predominantly distributed at consumer end. Therefore, wind power plants and PV generators in South Australia do not participate in frequency regulation. Under prolific penetration of wind and PV and considerable power ingress from adjoining system, an insignificant number of synchronous machines may be present in the South Australian network. During such condition, a big contingency (trip of an interconnection/a major generator) may result in unacceptable frequency response. Consequently, the network might face substantial under frequency load shedding. To mitigate this challenge, a solution for improving frequency response by taking into account the frequency control support from an HVDC interconnection is explored in this paper. To this end, a low inertia network, which mimics the South Australian grid, is analysed under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Physical understanding on the interface states and grain boundary defects of polysilicon nanowires
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper investigates effects of interface states and grain boundary defects on the electrical characteristics and provides insight into the nature of interface states and grain boundary defects of polysilicon nanowires (NWs) prepared by industry standard deposition and etch. It is found that acceptor-like interface states affect the leakage current whereas donor-like interface states affect both subthreshold and drive current characteristic of accumulation mode p-type polysilicon NW. Intrinsic grain boundary defects inside polysilicon exhibit quit interesting trend. The shallow acceptor or donor like states do not affect the electrical characteristics at all, whereas deep level acceptor like states significantly affect the leakage current. Deep level donor like states also significantly affect NW's subthreshold and drive current characteristic. The observed influence of location, type and energy level of defect states on the electrical characteristics of NW are used to calibrate the characteristic of p-type polysilicon NW fabricated by deposition and etch thereby provided a physical understanding on the nature of interface states and grain boundary defects of polysilicon nanowires.

articleTitle: First-principles study on strain engineered SnS monolayer
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Electronic properties of two-dimensional materials can be tuned with applied strain due to their ultrathin and flexible characteristics. In this work, we have performed first-principles calculations based on Density Functional Theory (DFT) to study the structural and electronic properties of SnS monolayer. SnS is semiconducting in nature with an indirect bandgap of 1.3815 eV. The electronic responses of the SnS monolayer to strain are found to be sensitive and anisotropic because of its puckered structure. It can be turned into a direct bandgap material with the applied strain and the bandgap is tunable within the energy range of 0.8752 eV to 1.7911 eVe It also experiences repeated indirect-direct bandgap transitions due to tensile uniaxial and biaxial strains. The carrier effective masses in the SnS monolayer are less sensitive to uniaxial strain but deviates a lot due to biaxial strain. In the region of direct transition, the electron and hole effective mass of strain engineered SnS monolayer varies from 0.19mo to 0.24m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> and 0.25mo to 0.36m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>, respectively. These intriguing properties make SnS monolayer a promising two-dimensional material for electronic and optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: FGMO Trial for frequency regulation in Bangladesh Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Load and generation balance exactly in nominal frequency is a rare phenomenon for any power system. Frequency regulation is to maintain the balance between demand and supply in real time. Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) is the transmission Grid operator for Bangladesh power system (BPS). PGCB tries to maintain a near real-time balance between generation and load and adjusts generation to manage power flows through interconnected transmission lines. PGCB do not have any primary or supplementary control for frequency regulation rather it does manually with the help of their own IP phone network. The frequency of BPS continuously fluctuates to a big extent because of absence of primary control (governor action) for frequency regulation. That's why the NLDC (National Load Dispatch Centre) of PGCB has a tendency to run the system at little bit higher than nominal frequency, so that they can be advantageous during contingencies. But operating power system in this way is waste of huge amount of primary energy. To overcome these difficulties, PGCB thought about free governor mode of operation (FGMO) and arranged a first time weeklong real-time trial on BPS for practical understanding about primary control for frequency regulation. In this Paper, an investigation is made on this trial to demonstrate frequency regulation and generator response by adopting Free Governor Mode of Operation.

articleTitle: Characterization of Multiwall Carbon Nanotube Thin Films Electrodeposited on Indium Tin Oxide Substrates
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Multiwall Carbon Nanotube (MWCNT) thin films were electrodeposited on Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) substrate. The effects of 0.1 % solutions of MWCNT incorporation in methanol with and without 1 mg red phosphorus doping were investigated. The electrodeposited MWCNT films were characterized by current density in methanol solution, SEM and UV-VIS-IR spectroscopy. During deposition in methanol solution a moderate current density in liquid phase was found. By incorporation of MWCNT in methanol the current density increases. The current density also increases by doping red phosphorus in methanol with and without MWCNT. In SEM micrographs, changes were observed in the electrodeposited films compared to pure ITO substrates. Red phosphorus doping make changes in SEM. From the UV - VIS-IR measurement it was observed that absorption increases using methanol in UV - VIS range but decreases in IR region from that of pure ITO. After doping red phosphorus in methanol absorption decreases all through UV-VIS-IR from that of pure ITO. By phosphorus doping with MWCNT, absorption decreases slightly from the films of undoped MWCNT. So the optoelectronic properties of the electrodeposited films are tunable by MWCNT incorporation on ITO substrates.

articleTitle: Specific Quality of Service Constrained Optimal Allocation of Transmit Power and Bits in NOMA Systhems
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This research work considers a downlink NOMA system where Base Station (BS) can communicate its single cognitive user through multiple channels as well as multiple users can be communicated through a single channel. Under such a system model, an optimization framework is proposed to determine transmit power and bits concurrently by employing multiobjective optimization problem to maximize the total bits and to minimize the total transmit power without degrading the Quality of Service (QoS). Simulation results show that, BS requires to broadcast with higher power in a channel with more noise power; whereas, bit allocation is higher in a channel with higher SINR and vice versa. The effects of changes in BER threshold, minimum bits requirement threshold, BS's power budget, upper bound on bits and number of users in the system are observed too on the allocation of BS's transmit power and bits.

articleTitle: Arsenic Removal Using Multiwall Carbon Nanotube
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Arsenic contamination for drinking water is still a great health hazardous issue for both developed and developing countries. Numerous techniques have been implemented for removing arsenic from drinking water. However, more emphasis has been given on the removal technique related to carbon nanotube absorbent. This study was aimed to investigate the adsorption as well as removal of arsenic using multiwall carbon nanotube as adsorbent or removing material. Arsenic contaminated water was treated in two ways: 1) Batch adsorption and 2) Column feeding system. Removal of arsenic in column technique was found better for each sample. Independent variables including carbon nanotubes dosage, contact time etc. were varied to determine the influence of these parameters on the removal capability of the arsenic from water. From this investigation it was evident that multiwall carbon nanotubes has the capability of adsorption or removal of arsenic. Moreover, it is possible to get water under safe limit using certain amount of nano materials and up to a certain level of contaminated water.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Non-invasive Continuous Blood Pressure Measurement and Monitoring System Using Photoplethysmography
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Non-invasive continuous blood pressure measurement has become very popular for hypertensive patients to prevent cardiovascular problems. Blood pressure readings are not continuous in the conventional cuff sphygmomanometer system. We have proposed microcontroller based non-invasive continuous blood pressure measurement technique in which no cuff is used and photoplethysmogram (PPG) signal is taken only from the finger. It gives no pain to human because no catheter is needed to insert inside the body. A sensor network consisting of light emitting diode and light dependent resistor is used to get a PPG signal by the volume oscillometric method. The variation of blood volume in the finger is measured by this optical sensor. The variation of blood volume changes to blood pressure linearly. Automatic multi-scale based peak detection algorithm is used to detect maximum and minimum peaks of continuous PPG signal which corresponds to systolic and diastolic pressure after some simplification. Our proposed system is controlled by Arduino Uno which has on-chip microcontroller ATmega328P. We measure continuous blood pressure with 30 seconds delay between adjacent readings for twelve subjects. The results are verified by conventional cuff sphygmomanometer system. The mean difference is less than ± 5 mmHg. Therefore, the proposed system is less expensive and gives quite reliable and more accurate results according to international standards.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach to Compensate Control Valve Stiction
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Automatic control system is very common in modern industrial plants. The performance of the control loop largely depends on the control valve. Stiction is a commonly found problem in control valve. It produces oscillation in process output and decreases the longevity of the control valve. Oscillatory responses of the control loops due to valve stiction can disturb process operation, degrade product quality and decrease plant profitability. So, it is important to provide an efficient technique to minimize the detrimental effects of a sticky control valve before it can be sent for maintenance. In this research work, a stiction compensation technique of control valve is developed by adding an extra pulse with detuned controller action for a certain period of time. The performance of the proposed compensator is analyzed and compared with other stiction compensators available in the literature.

articleTitle: Inrush Current Limiting of a Bridgeless AC- DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A simple inrush current limiting technique is presented here for hybrid resonant Pulse-Width Modulation bridgeless AC - DC power factor correction converter used in power supplies and battery charging units. The DC bus capacitor voltage is gradually increased to limit the charging current. As boost converter is not operated at high duty cycle, the PWM switch for gradual increase in voltage is incorporated with other PWM switches. The method used here is designed for the boost type converter but can be implemented on other type of converters as well. The technique also reduces spikes in current wave forms of traditional bridgeless AC-DC converters. The simulation is performed in MATLAB/SIMULINK. A comparison is also provided to show the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: BER Performance Analysis of an OFDM FSO Communication System over Atmospheric Turbulent Channel with Coherent Heterodyne Optical Receiver
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: FSO channel imposes enormous obstacles on adequate attainable performance levels because of its weather dependency which leads to system outages. In this paper a diagnostic methodology is introduced to assess the bit error rate performance of an OFDM FSO link using optical intensity modulation and coherent heterodyne optical detection receiver taking int° consideration the effect of sturdy atmospheric turbulence. The turbulence impact is demonstrated as gamma-gamma distribution and the performances are assessed as far as power penalty, CNR and BER endured by the framework because of the impact of turbulence at a given BER for a few framework parameters like turbulence quality, link separation, local oscillator control and so forth. It is discovered that with 4 subcarriers at 10 Gbps data rate, the power penalty is 6dB at a BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> for a for a connection separation of 3600 m with 1mW power of both RF and Optical local oscillator. Overall performance may be improved appreciably by way of growing the quantity of ofdm subcarriers.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of NiO-doped BaTiO3for Multilayer Ceramic Capacitor
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this research, NiO-doped BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(x = 0.0, 0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 wt %) smart ceramics were fabricated through a conventional solid-oxide technique. The effect of NiO incorporation into BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>also its micro-structure, phase and dielectric behaviors was explored by X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis, Field-emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) and LCR Analyzer. XRD analysis confirmed well crystalline tetragonal BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>phase without any secondary phase. Microstructure was found to controlled by grain growth inhabitation due to pinning effect of NiO at grain boundary especially at higher doping level (> 2 wt %). Diffuse and more stable dielectric properties were observed in NiO-doped sample compared to pure BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>counterpart. Enhanced dielectric properties with controlled microstructure may allow its application in multilayer ceramic capacitor.

articleTitle: Changing of Dielectric Properties Through Light-Matter Interaction Assisted by External Voltage
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: An external voltage has been applied across the capacitor configuration formed by two parallel aluminium plates with dielectric material in between, provides enough energy to the dielectric dipoles in order to shift the wavelength of the incident laser on that dielectric surface toward smaller values [1]. This change in optical property could be responsible for the change of relative permittivity of the dielectric surface which can be used as optical switch or waveguide. In this work, a flint glass prism is used as a dielectric medium whose index of refraction is 1.6242 and the Brewster angle is 58.388 degree for 532nm green diode laser.

articleTitle: A Classification Scheme for Predicting the Subcellular Localization of the Apoptosis Proteins Using Composition Features and Multiscale Entropy
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Apoptosis proteins carry out the mechanism of regulated cell destruction. To understand the process of apoptosis, it is important to classify the apoptosis proteins based on their subcellular location. Computer-assisted automatic detection of the subcellular location of the apoptosis proteins from their amino acid sequences can replace laboratory experiment which is both expensive and time-consuming. In this paper, the classification of apoptosis proteins based on their subcellular localization is presented. Various composition based features and multiscale entropy-based features are extracted. Neighborhood Component Analysis (NCA) is employed to select the features with high significance. Two well-known classifiers, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) and the K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) are employed to classify the proteins from the reduced feature set. The proposed method is validated using a widely used public database for apoptosis proteins. Well-known figures of merit such as accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and area under the curve (AUC) are analyzed and compared with state-of-the-art methods in the literature. It is seen that the proposed method shows promising results in terms of accuracy as well as sensitivity for each class and can be used as an automatic support system for researchers in identifying the subcellular location of apoptosis proteins.

articleTitle: Effects of Edge Termination on the Electronic Properties of Zigzag Boron Nitride Nanoribbons
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Two-dimensional hexagonal boron nitride has attracted the eyes of many scientists due to its very high thermal and electrical stability. This paper reports the effects of edge termination by non-metallic (NM) atoms (H, P, F, and O) on the electronic properties of zigzag boron nitride nanoribbon (ZBNNR). First principles calculations were performed using local density approximation (LDA) to calculate the electronic properties of ZBNNR. Several possible configurations have been considered such as ZBNNR with symmetric edge termination, asymmetric edge termination, and half bare edge. It was found that ZBNNR with O termination exhibits metallic property regardless of termination cases. ZBNNR with P termination exhibits semi-metallic massless dirac fermion behavior which is also independent of the termination cases. However, ZBNNR with H and F terminations exhibit metallic or semiconducting properties depending on the termination cases. These findings are very much important to understand the modulated electronic properties of ZBNNR as well as applications of these materials in nanoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Threshold Voltage Improvement of Enhancement-Mode Al2O3/ AIGaN/GaN MIS-HEMT with High Drain Current Density
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: We present an AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) operating in enhancement-mode (E-mode) with metal-insulator-semiconductor (MIS) structure showing improved threshold voltage. The design includes an aluminium gallium nitride (Alo.3Gao.7N) barrier layer of 5-nm-thickness and a silicon nitride (SiN) passivation layer. The passivation layer is used for controlling the charge density of electron gas in 2-dimension (2DEG). While aluminium oxide (Ah03) on AIGaN does not change the 2DEG charge density in the hetero-interface, it increases the threshold voltage in enhancement mode. MIS-HEMT operating in E-mode shows a peak drain-current density (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DS</sub>) of 975mA/mm and a threshold voltage (Vth) of 1.25 V. The drain current density can be increased with the increase of barrier layer charge concentration. On/off ratio and threshold voltage are compared with existing design available in literature. The significant improvement of device performance metrics can be done by controlling the charge concentration and the thickness of Alo.3Gao.7N barrier layer.

articleTitle: Design and Development of an Online Bus Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This research demonstrates the design and development of an online bus monitoring system. The primary purpose of the bus monitoring system is to track city buses for obtaining their location information. The proposed bus monitoring system consists of two fundamental sections: tracking the location of city buses and monitoring the city buses from website or android based phones. In order to monitor city buses, global positioning system (GPS) modules must be installed in the buses so that location information can be updated in the server. People can obtain the information of the city buses from the website of the bus monitoring system and using the android application of their android devices. The information regarding the location of any particular bus is obtained just within 40 seconds from both the website and android application. Although the proposed system is applicable in any cities of Bangladesh, we considered Khulna City as the model during our research. Furthermore, we analyze the performances in terms of response type and error for both website based and android application based systems under variable number of users. We strongly believe that our proposed bus monitoring system will be valuable to monitor the city buses of any city of Bangladesh.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Biochemical Sensor Using Multiple Cross-Slot Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Slot waveguides are generally unidirectional with an absence of strong confinement factor. This work presents an extraordinary way which contains both vertical and horizontal slots to make confinement factor very strong utilizing metal barriers around silicon cores to reflect electric fields which crosses high index silicon regions for both TE and TM polarizations. For a wavelength of 1550nm, the waveguide dimensions have been optimized to have equal confinement factor for both polarization which reaches to 59.30% with silicon core width, height and silver core width are set to 153nm, 257nm and 340nm respectively. Sensitivity analysis additionally demonstrates better performance contrasted with other single slot and cross-slot waveguides.

articleTitle: Effect of Halide Compositions on the Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this work, we present a simulation based study of perovskite solar cells to determine the best halide composition of methyl ammonium lead halide perovskite for the light absorbing layer of solar cells. We explore the performance of the two most commonly used configurations of perovskite solar cells: p-i-n and n-i-p and determine the halide composition of perovskite that yields the best results for each configuration. In addition, further optimization of the structures is attained in terms of different layer thicknesses, which leads to an increased efficiency of 17.78% and 16.43% for the p-i-n and n-i-p architectures, respectively.

articleTitle: Thermal Transport in Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Using Equilibrium Molecular Dynamics Simulation
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The thermal transport property of armchair graphene nanoribbons (GNRs) is studied employing equilibrium molecular dynamics (EMD) simulation based on Green-Kubo (GK) method with optimized Tersoff interatomic potential and original Tersoff potential. The calculated room temperature thermal conductivity of 10 nmx3 nm armchair graphene nanoribbon is ~1300 W/m-K. Our study comprises of the impact of temperature and width on thermal conductivity of armchair GNRs. The investigation shows a decreasing trend of the thermal conductivity with the increase of temperature. Corresponding phonon density of states (PDOS) curves show red shift at elevated temperatures. Thermal conductivity is found to increase with the increasing width of GNRs. Total acoustic PDOS at different sample width showed presence of higher energy phonons at wider GNRs. A comparative study shows that original Tersoff Potential underestimates thermal conductivity than those with optimized Tersoff interatomic potential. Such study would provide a detail insight of thermal transport in graphene nanoribbons.

articleTitle: IMPACT: Image processing based Maze solver, Persistent Autonomous object Carrying boT
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Object categorization and transportation holds a significant position in the repertoire of tasks performed in industries every day. Thus the utility of automating this process is manifold. Nowadays, in industrial environments robust communication and image acquisition setup is present for monitoring and security purposes. Our motivation was to use this sensor network and build a lightweight, real-time, simple yet reliable object carrying system. We hereby present a prototype of an automated system, that with some little prior knowledge about the assigned task can adapt itself in a variable environment and perform the task successfully. The complete software and hardware system had been developed and was experimented intensively.

articleTitle: Stabilization Improvement of Load Frequency Deviation for Multi-Area Interconnected Smart Grid Using Integral Linear Quadratic Gaussian Control Approach
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper proposes integral linear quadratic Gaussian (ILQG) control approach for frequency stabilization of multi-area connected smart grid. This controller is designed based on multi-area tie-in smart grid populated with PHEVs. The controller is improved version of linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) controller with an integral action. The motivation for designing the controller is to stabilize the frequency deviation in an acceptable range. The performance is evaluated using Matlab Simulink. The results show that the ILQG controller ensures high performance for frequency stabilization of multiarea interconnected smart grid.

articleTitle: RF Pilot Tone Based Photonic Pattern Recognition
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper a novel technique to perform photonic pattern recognition using RF pilot tones is proposed. To improve the detection sensitivity, the detection of matched and mismatched condition is done in electrical domain. The reference bit patterns are represented by RF pilot tones on optical wavelengths. Different wavelengths are modulated with both reference and input bit patterns using Mach Zehnder Modulator and then passed through a Highly Nonlinear Fiber (HNLF). Due to the nonlinear properties of the HNLF, new frequency components will be generated by RF pilot tones. A matched pattern is designated by detecting a unique RF frequency which is the summation of RF pilot tones at the photodetector (PD). We demonstrate a matched filter which provides high signal to noise ratio (SNR) and high contrast between matched and mismatched conditions.

articleTitle: Temperature Induced Localization Dynamics of Exciton in ZnO/MgZnO and CdZnO/MgZnO Quantum Well
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The localization dynamics of photo-generated excitons in ZnO/MgZnO and CdZnO/MgZnO quantum wells (QWs) are studied using the Monte Carlo simulation of exciton hoping for the temperature range of 5 to 300K. The simulated result is compared with the experimental photoluminescence (PL) data and a reasonable agreement is found for the whole range of temperature. A remarkable effect of phonon-induced change of excitons radiative lifetime on the PL peak energy positions and line-width is observed. At high temperature, the redshift behavior of PL peak energy positions is clarified. The temperature dependence of the PL line-widths in both ZnO/MgZnO and CdZnO/MgZnO QWs has been explained quantitatively for the entire range of temperature. These results are expected to be very useful for future ZnO based electronic and optoelectronic devices.

articleTitle: Words to Meaningful Sentence: Analytics through Game Interface
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this work, we designed an experiment to discover the sentence making process followed by a human. To achieve the goal of meaningful sentence construction with a context by the computer, it requires an efficient algorithm. The computer can identify visual elements of a scene through the convolutional neural network. These visual elements are a few important words in a whole sentence. A human being constructs a meaningful sentence with such visual elements by incorporating connecting words which is not yet plausible by the computer. The typical generative deep models generate sentences which many times does not follow the context because the methods of sentence construction by a human (i.e., interpolation of connecting words) are less studied. This research is an attempt to have a better idea of the words interpolation. This will be useful to devise an efficient algorithm for image description generation especially for the useful application of visually impaired or blind people.

articleTitle: Living Machines
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Industrial revolution of the 19th century marked the onset of the era of machines that transformed societies. However, all of these machines are non-living, and they do not have inherent intelligence. On the other hand, since the discovery of genes, there is a considerable body of knowledge on engineering living cells. It is thus appropriate to envision biohybrid micro machines that are made from microfabricated scaffolds and living cells. These machines have the potential of unprecedented capabilities, as they would carry the footprints of millions of years of evolution. These machines may emerge from an interaction between the living cells and the micro-nano scaffolds. Thus, they might be the unique products of both the bottom-up and top-down methods. In this talk we will present such an elementary micro machine consisting of a soft slender string and rat cardiomyocytes. The string is made from PDMS by filling a microfabricated channelusing capillary draw. Cells are cultured on one region of the string. These cells interact with the string as well as with each other, and beat in synchrony as a single actuator. This living actuator bends the string, and a bending wave propagates from the actuator site towards the end, as a bending of a sperm. This artificial machine thus swims in fluids as the engineered living swimmer. These swimmers might be used in vivo for autonomous intelligent drug delivery.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of 12 Channel Electrocardiogram Device
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper a cost effective Electrocardiogram machine has been proposed and successfully implemented. Electrocardiogram signal is a very low voltage (10uV to 5mV whose typical value is 1mV)signal generated by the heart, which is multiple times bellow the noise level. Movement of different internal organs also create different types of noise. Different types of filters and amplifiers are used to remove the unexpected signals and to amplify the expected signal to get the desired signal. Finally ECG machine has been developed and successfully experimented on human body.

articleTitle: Wideband Arrays with Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Future wireless communication systems will require much higher data rates. Suhc high rates require wideband arrays with beam forming capabilities. Concurrently, the RF spectrum will become more vulnerable due to intentional and unintentional interference. Therefore, interference cancellation and mitigation techniques as well as low cost wideband beamformers are required to ensure high gain secure communication for 5G commercial applications and for government needs.

articleTitle: Advanced Control Scheme for Bidirectional Grid-Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A design of voltage & current control system for the grid-connected inverter is proposed here. The controller can also be used for energy storage systems (ESSs). The voltage control system represented in this paper is based on an adaptive PI controller which provides very low dc-link voltage fluctuations & fast transient response. The current control strategy used here can optimize the transient error & eliminate steady-state error. Simulations are performed on MATLAB Simulink. The effectiveness of the designed system is checked by comparing the simulation results with the results available in the literature. The proposed system can be used for improving the transient response of the grid-connected bidirectional inverters.

articleTitle: Cost Effective Perovskite Solar Cell with Inorganic Hole- Transporting Material
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Perovskite solar cell (PSC) with inorganic hole-transporting material is cost effective and stable. This paper presents a numerical analysis of CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>PbI<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> based PSC using SCAPS-1D software. Actual absorption spectra of different layers of the PSC structure are considered in the analysis. The performance of the reference PSC has been investigated by varying the absorber layer thickness. It has been found that the efficiency is maximized when the absorber thickness is reduced. The doping densities of different layers are also varied to increase the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of the PSC. The proposed structure achieves a PCE of 14.63% where PCE increases by 1.9% in comparison with the reference cell. The proposed structure shows a short-circuit current (J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</sub>) of21.17 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an open circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.07V, and a fill factor of 64.38% under global AM 1.5 condition. The reduced absorber thickness, as well as the improved efficiency, makes the proposed PSC structure cost effective and efficient.

articleTitle: Flyback AC-DC Rectifier with Active Power Factor Correction
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A new topology of flyback AC-DC rectifier with power factor correction and low total harmonic distortion (THD) in the input current has been proposed in this paper. The proposed flyback rectifier has a single stage AC-DC conversion, combining the rectification process and DC-DC conversion only in one step, resulting in higher efficiency, effective power factor correction and input current harmonic distortion reduction. The system does not have tertiary winding or snubber circuit so it results in reduction of transformer size of the conventional circuit. The proposed design along with power factor corrected feedback circuit has been compared with the conventional designs available in the literatures and the proposed circuit's performance is found more satisfactory in terms of input current THD (%), efficiency (%) and input power factor.

articleTitle: Reduction of Radiation Exposure from Cellular Base Stations by Joint Time Scheduling and Power Controlling
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Radiation hazard from rapidly increasing base stations (BSs) of cellular networks is a burning issue of the day. In this paper, the problem of reduction of radiation from mobile phone BSs is considered. First, a traditional cellular system is considered where the transmit power at the BSs is fixed. For the traditional system, the radiation exposure to the cell phone users is determined by using an analytical model. It is found that the radiation exposure to the users does not exceed the related IEEE standards but it is higher than the precautionary limits set in some countries. It is also found that a user receives most of the radiation power from its nearest BS and the increment of radiation exposure for reducing the antenna height is significant to those users who are suffering higher radiation. Next, a power control and user scheduling scheme is proposed to reduce the radiation exposure to the users. Analytical models are developed to configure the transmit power and user scheduling parameters for reducing the power density to the users by satisfying the traffic of the users. A model to calculate the power density to the users under the proposed scheme is also developed. The performance of the proposed scheme is evaluated and compared with the traditional scheme. Comparison results show that the reduction of the power density to the mobile phone users by the proposed scheme is remarkable.

articleTitle: Comparative Performance Analysis Between CIGS Single-Junction and CIGS Tandem Multi-Junction Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: We present a comparative study between CIGS tandem and CIGS single-junction solar cells. The solar cell parameters like open circuit voltage, short circuit current density, fill factor, maximum power and external quantum efficiency are compared. Calculations use the standard software tool SILVACO ATLAS. We first optimize the structure of the tandem solar cell by varying the thickness of each layer and then compare the results with the single junction cells. The open circuit voltage of the tandem and single junction cells is almost same, however, the tandem cell is approximately 14% more efficient and it provides 12% more current than the single junction cells.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Analysis of Multijunction Organic Solar Cell Exceeding 14% Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this report, we propose the design of a novel triple junction solar cell composed of two organic and one organic-inorganic materials namely, PTB7:PCBM, PMDPP3T:PCBM and Perovskite. We initially optimize the thicknesses of the three active materials simultaneously from opto-electronic simulation. Then we estimate the overall performance of the entire structure from circuit solution using diode model of the solar cell. We have found out that the optimized layer thicknesses are 150 nm, 150 nm and 700 nm respectively. At these thicknesses, the cell efficiency reaches up to 14.69% with open circuit voltage, short circuit current density and fill factor being 1.859 V, 10.12 mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and 78.13% respectively.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Scaling Effects of a Double Gate Silicon and In0.47Ga0.53As MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Nowadays technology keeps progressing and device becomes smaller for fast processing. With small dimensions the quantum mechanical effects become prominent and the device performance degrades due to severe short channel effects such as threshold voltage roll off. We study the device dimensions' effects on the performance of a double gate MOSFET for both Si and In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>As channels using energy balance model with Bohm quantum potential of Silvaco simulation tool. For a 2 nm SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gate oxide with 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>source-drain doping density, the device threshold voltage close to 1.0 V and 0.57 V for Si and In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>As respectively up to channel length of = 40 nm, below which the threshold voltage falls off rapidly. The channel body thickness and oxide thickness affect the threshold voltage when the channel length is below 40 nm. We observe similar dimension effects on sub-threshold slope, DIBL and ON current for both Si and In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.47</sub>Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.53</sub>As.

articleTitle: Challenges And Opportunities of Renewable Energy Integrations to National Grids
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Many countries around the world are promoting renewable energy generations to address climate change and to reduce carbon emissions. Among them, solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind power are making significant proliferations in distribution and transmission networks. Solar PV generation is variable and wind power generation is intermittent and hence they bring many challenges for network and overall energy management. University of Queensland Power & Energy Systems research group are involved in a number of solar PV and wind projects, which are progressing towards addressing some of the major challenges the electricity industry is currently facing. This seminar will outline some key outcomes from our research projects to address the challenges and opportunities from renewable energy integrations.

articleTitle: Hybrid Plasmon Waveguide for Capacitor Like Energy Localization in Dielectric Gap
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A hybrid plasmon waveguide comprising with metal and dielectric nanowires has been investigated employing the finite element method. At the telecommunication wavelength, strong SPP-dielectric mode coupling in this structure gives rise to capacitor like electromagnetic energy localization in the dielectric gap with extremely low effective area (~λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/600) and appreciable propagation length. Apart from the fundamental gap mode, the structure has been reported to excite a long ranging hybrid mode with moderate mode size. The feasibility of this structure has been explored in different nanophotonic applications considering the derived modal parameters.

articleTitle: Design And Optimization of Emerging Photonic Sensors
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Summary form only given. Although optical sensors using side polished or etched optical fibres, metal coated for plasmonic resonances, and incorporating Bragg grating are now sufficiently mature and well established in the market, however, designs based on more exotic nanowires and photonic crystal fibres are becoming increasingly important and showing much improved sensitivity by accessing a larger evanescent field. Similarly, novel planar design concepts, such as the silicon slot guide-based design is showing even greater promise, allowing the exploitation of well-developed CMOS fabrication technologies for potentially low-cost sensor elements. In compact Integrated Optic format, dielectric slots, plasmonic slots, Mach-Zehnder interferometer, and ring resonators are also emerging as potential optical sensors of the future.

articleTitle: Development of Simulation Model of a Controlled Rectifier for Reactive Power Compensation
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Total harmonic distortion(THD) caused by conventional controlled and un-controlled rectifiers decreases power factor(PF) degrading power quality of the grid. Controlled rectifier using space vector pulse width modulated (SVPWM) signals can be a good candidate to overcome the THD limitation of conventional rectifiers. In this paper, an 30V AC-to-12-V/12A 144W SVPWM rectifier circuit with necessary gate pulse generation technique has been modeled and simulated in Simulink to verify the operation of the rectifier in purpose of future implementation in hardware system. SVPWM controlled rectifiers have the capability of drawing sinusoidal input currents with proper input filtering as well as phase shift control and thus can control the overall PF of the system. These important characteristics have been verified in the built simulation model and reported in this paper. Also, a pulse sequence have been developed which can be directly used to build hardware systems.

articleTitle: Multiheaded starfish shaped multiband microstrip patch antenna for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This study concerns a simulation of a multiheaded starfish shaped patch antenna for satellite communication as the primary purpose. The proposed antenna can operate over the frequency bands of 3.025-3.057 GHz, 7.7716GHz-7.88GHz, 9.005GHz-9.225GHz, 10.06GHz-10.27GHz. The S11 = -10 dB impedance bandwidth is 32 MHz (3.025-3.057 GHz), 108.4 MHz (7.7716GHz-7.88GHz), 220 MHz (9.005GHz-9.225GHz), 210 MHz (10.06GHz-10.27GHz). The resonant frequencies are 3.04 GHz, 7.81 GHz, 9.13 GHz, 10.18 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Quadruple Decimal Logarithmic Converter
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a high precision Quadruple (128-bit) decimal logarithmic converter. It has been designed using IEEE industry standard Verilog HDL and simulated using ModelSim software. It is the first of its kind that uses a 128-bit floating-point arithmetic for high precision. Desired functionality and accuracy of the converter have been tested using different test data. The converter is low power and low logic gate counts since digit-by-digit iterative technique that does not require look-up tables, curve fitting, decimal-binary conversion, or division operations has been used. Finally the accuracy of the converter has been tested with that of CASIO calculator which shows that the result is correct up to 34-digit. It has also been compared with that of other researchers which shows its superior performance in terms of precision.

articleTitle: Microstrip-Line Fed Gap-Coupled Antennas for Different Patch Geometries
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, we present various microstrip-line fed gap-coupled antennas for different patch-geometries. A single shorting post with a pair of λ / 4 resonator and a radiating patch have been used in the antenna to obtain improved Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR). We have proposed 5 different patch-geometries - square, rectangle, pentagon, trigonal pentagon, five-spoked star - which exhibit superior bandwidth and VSWR properties in the 4-7 GHz frequency range. The proposed antennas occupy a small space and have been simulated on a 1.6 mm thick ArIon Substrate. The (VSWR) for the five proposed patch-geometries have been simulated, and, their radiation patterns have been compared across the VSWR ≤ 2 bandwidth.

articleTitle: GeO2 Doped Polarization Maintaining Fiber for Residual Dispersion Compensation
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this article, proposed photonic crystal fiber is GeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> doped elliptical core with asymmetric shaped hexagonal clad to attain ultra-flattened negative dispersion with high birefringence. From the simulation results, it is found that in the cladding using circular and elliptical air holes combination, Gaining large average dispersion of -856.15 ps/nm/km is possible with a dispersion variation of 8 ps/nm/km over S+C+L+U optical band of interest for the fundamental slow axis mode. Tailoring the design parameters in optimum level, a high birefringence of 6.65×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> and a nonlinearity of 70.87 W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>at 1.55 μm wavelength. Our considered structure is very effective for residual dispersion compensation. It could be used in the optical sensor, high bit rate coherent communication, and as a polarization maintaining fiber because of its high birefringence.

articleTitle: Influence of Sintering Temperature on Magnetic Characteristics of Li-Cu-Ni-Zn Ferrite
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The ferromagnetic Li<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l0</sub>CU<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>.<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">lO</sub>Nio.<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</sub>Zno.<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4o</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.1</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>synthesized by the typical ceramic technique which is sintered at the various temperatures. The formation of single phase cubic spinel structure at varied sintering temperatures (T <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>) is confirmed by the x-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis. XRD pattern confirms that the T <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>does not distress the inner structure of the sample. The bulk density and theoretical density are found to be improved with T <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>. Due to increasing of T s, a normal fast grain growth happens over the pores volume which reduced the porosity with sample density. The value of relative quality factor (RQF) and initial permeability are also enhanced with T <sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>because of low porosity and high density. The peaks of the relative quality factor are shifted toward to the left with the T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>which indicates the decreasing trend of the loss factor. The characteristics of structural, density, porosity, relative quality factor, initial permeability and loss factor of the composition are explained here.

articleTitle: Reduction of Excitation Volume in Fluorescence Spectroscopy with Localized Surface Plasmon
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: By introducing a sub-wavelength square nanohole in a semitransparent thin silver film, the penetration depth and the propagation length of the evanescent field can be reduced remarkably, confining the excitation field to a very small region. The excitation volume in the proposed structure is reduced to only 1.8% of the analyte volume excited in the conventional fluorescence spectroscopy structure based on surface plasmon coupled emission (SPCE) technique. Additionally, the proposed structure does not require hemispherical glass substrate for the wavevector match, since normally incident light beam can excite the surface plasmon mode at the aperture walls, rendering the device size to micrometer scale. Moreover, for the optimized dimensions of the nanohole, the peak excitation field is found to be ~3.3 times stronger than the peak evanescent field obtainable in the conventional arrangements. With reduced device size, increased resolution and enhanced field strength, the proposed structure will find applications in chip array implementation of florescence microscopy, and variants of SPCE based single molecule detection (SMD).

articleTitle: Atomistic Simulation and Compact Modeling of Atomically Thin Transistors
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, we show the impact of channel thickness scaling on material and transistor behavior. we present effect of the strain on energy bandgap in scaled Si and Ge slabs for varying thickness. For lower effective mass III-V channel materials, influence of the lower density of states and contribution of multiple subbands on the gate capacitance and drain current in thin body metal-oxide-semiconductor devices are discussed using the numerical simulation and compact model. We present doping strategy for monolayer MoS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> to increase free charge carrier density to increase drive current in MoS2 based transistors. We also discuss compact modeling approach for 2D transition metal dichalcogenide materials-based transistors for early circuit evaluation.

articleTitle: Adaptation of Transmit Power and Bits/Subchannel in QoS Constrained Downlink Cognitive OFDMA Networks
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper investigates an optimal allocation of transmit power and bits/subchannel for OFDM-based downlink CR system. The aim is to construct an optimization framework for OFDM-based downlink CR system that jointly maximizes the bits/subchannel and minimizes its transmit power while maintaining quality of service (QoS) and total transmit power limit. The measures for QoS include bit error rate (BER) and minimum rate requirement. Numerical results reveal the performance of the proposed scheme. Equivalence between power consumption-bits/subchannel trade-off and EE-SE trade-off of the system is also studied.

articleTitle: Resurrection of DC: An exposition for Future Power System
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Historical background of AC and DC are presented and the changing scenario with the development of power electronics are pointed out. Advantages of DC systems in generation, transmission-distribution and consumption are discussed in the context of the existing AC system. A DC power system schematic is proposed and the main challenges with possible solutions in this regard are discussed.

articleTitle: Performance of the Noise Subspace-Based Estimation Algorithm for Correlated Sources
publicationTitle: 2018 10th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The NoIse Subspace-based Estimation (NISE) algorithm has been shown to provide adequate direction of arrival (DoA) estimates for uncorrelated sources in traditionally difficult scenarios, with relatively low computational complexity. In this work, we discuss the behavior of NISE in practical scenarios where the sources are correlated, and provide a mathematical proof of its convergence. Numerical results showing the performance of NISE against Unitary Root-MUSIC are also presented.
